podcast.title: Website Last Updated 2005
podcast.body: As of the transcript's information, Gaynell Hodge's website had not been updated since 2005, with its most recent news mentioning his collaboration with Dr. John on a song for Shemekia Copeland. "His website hasn't been updated since 2005, but at the time, its most recent news flash was that he had co-written this song with Dr. John for Shemik here co-plum."

podcast.title: Appearance on "Al Yoop"
podcast.body: Hodge played piano on the novelty record "Al Yoop" by The Hollywood Argales. "Al Yoop, under the name The Hollywood R Gales, which featured Gaynell Hodge on piano."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Bridge Between Black R&B and White Pop Scenes
podcast.body: Hodge served as one of the few links between the Black R&B musicians of the 1950s and the white-dominated Los Angeles pop music scene of the 1960s, which included genres like surf, hot rods, folk rock, and sunshine pop. "He was also one of the few links between that 50s world of Black R&B musicians, and the white dominated 60s LA pop music scene of surf, hot rods, folk rock, and sunshine."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Central Avenue Music Scene Involvement
podcast.body: Gaynell Hodge was an active figure in the Central Avenue music scene in Los Angeles, an area Sam Cooke frequented while waiting for Keen Records to launch. "Sam made himself firmly a part of the central avenue music scene, hanging around with Gaynell Hodge, Jesse Belvin, Dutti Williams, Guggi Renne, John Dolphin, and everyone else who was part of the LAR and B community."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Claims Regarding Alex Hodge's Departure
podcast.body: Gaynell Hodge asserts that the official reason for his brother Alex Hodge's departure from The Platters (marijuana possession) was a fabrication. He claims Book Ram and Herb Reed conspired to remove Alex because Alex, the alleged original founder of the group, was too knowledgeable about the music business and was becoming suspicious of Ram's financial dealings. "Gael Hodge now claims that this wasn't the real reason that Alex Hodge was sacked."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Dual Membership with The Hollywood Flames
podcast.body: Gaynell Hodge was a member of The Flamingos (which became The Platters) and also simultaneously a member of The Hollywood Flames. He eventually left The Platters to focus solely on The Hollywood Flames. "Gaynell Hodge, who was also in the Hollywood flames at the same time."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Last Surviving Original Platter
podcast.body: Gaynell Hodge is identified as the last surviving member of the original Platters lineup. He continues to perform with his own Platters group, even singing songs recorded after his departure from the main group. "Gain L. Hodge, however, is still alive, the last surviving member of the original platters."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Major Figure in California Music Industry
podcast.body: Gaynell Hodge is recognized as a major figure within the California music industry, with expectations of his involvement appearing in future historical accounts and important records. "Gain L. Hodge was a major figure in the California music industry."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Pivotal Figure in 50s LA Vocal Group Scene
podcast.body: Gaynell Hodge was one of the most important people in the 1950s Los Angeles vocal group scene. His contributions were so fundamental that without him, groups like The Platters, The Penguins, and Jesse Belvin would not have existed. "Gainl Hodge was one of the most important people in the 50s LA vocal group scene, and without him there would have been no platters, penguins, or Jesse Bellvin."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Recent Death (Week of Episode)
podcast.body: Gaynell Hodge's death occurred during the week the episode was being written. "As I was in the middle of writing this episode, I received word that Hodge had died earlier this week."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
